Page 1/5 
Machine Learning (BMI/GEO/WNA) 
Code Assignment U1A1  
Linear Regression 
This is NOT a group Assignment. 
 
10 marks 
Please complete seeing the videos for Week 1-2 before attempting this 
assignment.  
Use real estate valuation regression dataset : 
https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/477/real+estate+valuation+data+set  from 
the UCI repository, and use google colab to code. 
First, download the csv file, and open it in your computer and analyze the data. 
Try to understand what the data is about. Read through the data description 
given 
in 
the 
UCI 
website 
as 
well. 
Section A 
Answer the following questions [1 mark if you answer all the below questions] 
: 
1. How many samples are there? 
414 
 
2. How many input variables are there? 
6 
 
3. Which column is the output variable (target outcome)? 
Y house price of unit area 
 
 
4. What does each of the input columns mean ? 
X1 transaction date: Date of purchase of the real estate. 
X2 house age: how old the house is, to assume the life span of the house. 
X3 distance to the nearest MRT station: How close the nearest metro is, how 
close the mode of transport is, which would help if they are someone who 
uses the metro a lot.

Page 2/5 
X4 number of convenience stores: to check if the neighborhood is good or 
has services for grocery shopping in case they run out off any ingredients. 
X5 and X6, the latitude and longitude to mark the exact location of the house. 
Y house price of unit area: to check if the price of the house matches the 
available services provided by it and its neighborhood. 
 
 
Section B 
For each of the questions below, you need to put in the screenshot of the code 
and its output. You could use the sample google colab file that is provided with 
this assignment. 
1. Understanding the dataset [4 marks] 
There are many input variables in this dataset. Use only X1 to X4 as input 
variables, and y as the output variable. 
Using the scatter plots between each of the input features (X1-X4) and the 
output (Y), which input variable, do you think, is better in predicting the output 
/ target variable ?

Page 3/5 
 
 
X3 would be the best input variable for predicting Y house price of unit area as 
the output/target variable. 
Here, X3 distance to the nearest metro station has better fit compared to the 
rest because of the clustering we can observe from the given scatter plot. Other 
than x3, we can also use x2 house age and x4 number of convenience stores in 
the neighborhood since they significant and slight decrease in price. 
 
2. Write code to find out how many samples are there in total in this dataset? [1 
mark]

Page 4/5 
 
3. What is the train test split ratio that you have chosen ? [1 Mark] 
70:30 
 
 
4. Evaluate the linear regression model by computing the MAE, MSE and Mean 
Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) . 
(for MAPE - pls refer to the sample here - https://scikit-
learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.mean_absolute_percent
age_error.html)  
[3 marks]

Page 5/5 
5. What are the 3 new things that you learned after you completed this 
assignment ? 
- Finding the best fit from a set of multiple input variables, where anything could 
be considered as input variable.  
- Selecting 70:30 train test split ratio, this implies the use of 70% of the data for 
training and 30% for testing. The choice of the split ratio depends on the size of 
the dataset. For relatively small datasets, a 70:30 split is considered suitable. 
- Calculate the mean absolute percent error.
